Leeds City Council elections

Find information about Leeds City Council elections, which can include details of vacancies, nominations, polling station locations, candidates and their agents.

Cross Gates and Whinmoor by-election

Notice of vacancy

I must give notice, under Section 87(2)(b) of the Local Government Act 1972, that a vacancy exists in the office of City Councillor for the Cross Gates and Whinmoor ward of Leeds City Council.

For a by-election to be held to fill the vacancy, a written request made by 2 registered local government electors in the Leeds City Council area must be given to:

Ed Whiting
Proper Officer
c/o Electoral Services
Civic Hall
Leeds
LS1 1UR

electors@leeds.gov.uk  

On receipt of a valid request, the Returning Officer will set the date of an election to be held within 35 days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays), in accordance with Section 89(1)(b) of the Local Government Act 1972.

Ed Whiting
Proper Officer 

Dated: 2 November 2026

Calverley and Farsley by-election

A by-election was held in the Calverley and Farsley Ward on Thursday 22 October 2026.

Declaration of result

I, Ed Whiting, being Returning Officer for election of a councillor to the Calverley and Farsley Ward of Leeds City Council, held on Thursday 22 October 2026 hereby give notice that the number of votes recorded for each candidate is as follows:

Name of candidate Description (if any) Number of votes
BUXTON, Robert Charles commonly known as BUXTON, Bob Yorkshire Party 57
CARTER, Amanda Lesley The Conservative Party Candidate 2,330 (Elected)
GABBITAS, Craig Reform UK 693
GILPIN, Daisy Nikita Green Party 341
HOLMES, Bradley Evan Restore Britain 151
MCLEOD, Stuart Liberal Democrats 92
PENNY, Kathryn Sara Labour and Co-operative Party 2,134

The number of ballot papers rejected was as follows:

Rejection reason Number of ballot papers
(a) want of official mark 0
(b) voting for more candidates than the voter is entitled to 2
(c) being unmarked or void for uncertainty 4
(d) writing or mark by which the voter can be identified 0
Total 6

I therefore declare that Amanda Lesley Carter has been elected as councillor for the Calverley and Farsley Ward of Leeds City Council.

Ed Whiting OBE
Returning Officer

Friday 23 October 2026

Turnout: 32.20%

How local elections work in Leeds

Every Leeds City Council ward is represented by 3 councillors who are each elected to serve a 4 year term. Their terms are staggered so that we only select one councillor in each local election. This system is called voting by thirds because a third of councillors are elected each year, over a 4 year cycle. Due to this, once every 4 years there are no local elections. This is called a fallow year. The next fallow year in Leeds is 2029.

In 2018 we elected 3 councillors in each ward. This is because the ward boundaries had been independently reviewed to reflect changes in population and ensure each ward contains a similar amount of electors. It is likely there won’t be another ward boundary review in Leeds for around 15 years.

The next scheduled elections will be the Leeds City Council elections which will be held on Thursday 6 May 2027.
